# Deployment Core

> A public evidence layer for U.S. nuclear deployment. It tracks which companies
> are building new-design reactors, how far each has actually got, and what
> document proves it. Every number on the site links to a source.

Data as of 2026-11-19. This is a tracked sample, not a census.

## What the site measures

Companies race to put one gigawatt of new-design nuclear on the U.S. grid.
Each company's capacity is split into bands by how strong the evidence is.
A megawatt sits in exactly one band, so the bands never double-count.

- **Operational** (0 MWe, 0 companies): Grid-connected and generating commercial power. Granting authority: Grid operator.
- **Nuclear construction** (345 MWe, 1 company): NRC construction permit issued and physical nuclear work documented. Granting authority: NRC.
- **DOE-authorized build** (75 MWe, 1 company): Built under a DOE authorization pathway with physical work documented. Not an NRC license to operate. Granting authority: DOE.
- **NRC permitted** (620 MWe, 2 companies): Construction permit issued; physical nuclear work not yet documented in the tracked evidence. Separate operating license still required. Granting authority: NRC.
- **Under review** (680 MWe, 1 company): Construction-permit or combined-license application docketed and in active regulator review. Granting authority: NRC.
- **Contracted** (336 MWe, 2 companies): An executed, funded agreement for a named project, whether offtake, order, delivery, or development funding, not yet in regulator review. Each claim says which kind it is. Granting authority: Counterparty.
- **Announced, non-binding** (37,060 MWe, 13 companies): MOU, LOI, master agreement, or announced target. No executed project documents. Granting authority: None.

## U.S. commercial fleet baseline

2025: 94 year-end operable units, 96880 MWe net summer capacity, 784.781 TWh annual net generation, 17.7% of U.S. electricity, 91% published capacity factor. Source: https://www.eia.gov/totalenergy/data/browser/csv.php?tbl=T08.01
Publication: October 2026. Stocks and annual flows have different denominators. See https://pranava0x0.github.io/nucleardeployment/fission for five years and all reactor families.

## Selected advanced-reactor sample totals

- No entrant in this selected new-design sample has generated a commercial megawatt. Sample operational capacity is 0 MWe; this is not national nuclear output.
- 420 MWe is physically under construction.
- 2,056 MWe rests on an executed action of any kind, including applications filed.
- 37,060 MWe has been announced without binding documents.
- Announced capacity is about 18x everything executed, and about 88x what is being built.

## Rules that govern the numbers

- Binding and non-binding capacity are never added together.
- Test reactors and critical experiments count 0 MWe. A criticality proves the
  physics works. It is not electricity and not a licence to sell any.
- A company-stated target never moves a megawatt between bands. Only a
  documented action does.
- U.S. megawatts only. The same design built abroad counts 0 MWe here.
- A DOE authorization is not an NRC licence. The bands keep them apart.

## Financing layer

Costs, contracts, and underwriters, every figure sourced and estimates kept
apart from facts. FOAK is a first-of-a-kind unit; NOAK the nth after learning.
- 12 cost benchmarks by reactor class, spanning completed-plant actuals, study estimates, and company targets.
- 14 contracting mechanisms in use with executed examples, plus 6 mechanisms available or pending without an executed instance, and 2 proposals.
- 7 underwriting institutions and 2 pooled liability structures.
- Full layer: https://pranava0x0.github.io/nucleardeployment/financing

## BD layer

Who buys new nuclear, by reactor class and sector, on a ladder that keeps
executed deals, equity stakes, prepayments, frameworks, programs, and
statements apart. Sector plans are the site's labeled judgment.
- 43 tracked buyers across 8 sectors, holding 70 sourced positions.
- 8 documented rungs on the path from microreactor criticalities to a factory cadence.
- Full layer: https://pranava0x0.github.io/nucleardeployment/bd

## Where the evidence comes from

Every record names who reported it, in the order the methodology ranks them:
- Verified: 8 records
- Government-reported: 16 records
- Institution-reported: 1 records
- Company-reported: 34 records
- Press-reported: 18 records

- Verified means the regulator's own record, such as a Federal Register notice.
- Press-reported is a real source, but it is never the best one available when
  the company or the regulator published the same fact.
